Scoring a rule on the cells left unrun is confounded: different rules reveal different benchmarks, so their targets differ and the target changes with $k$ (a rule that reveals the hardest benchmarks removes them from its own target and can score below the floor). We therefore split the 328 benchmarks at random into a pool $C$ of 219, from which a rule may choose, and a target set $T$ of 109 that no rule can choose, stratified by task type. For each held-out model the run set $S\subseteq C$ is chosen among the benchmarks the model has in $C$, and every rule and every inference method is scored on the model's observed cells in $T$. The floor is the same prediction with all of the model's observed cells in $C$ revealed. A pair (model, split) is eligible if the model has at least $k$ observed cells in $C$ and at least $\lceil 109/3\rceil=37$ in $T$; a model enters the curve at $k$ if it is eligible in at least 20 of 50 fixed splits, which are shared by all models, folds and rules. The headline curve uses the models that enter at the largest $k$, so the set of models does not change along the axis; the curve over all models eligible at each $k$ is a supplement. The margins $\delta_j$ below are averaged over the model's observed cells in $T$. Scores on the unrun cells, without a pool and target, are reported as a secondary and labelled as such.
$F_T(S)=\sum_{j\in T}v_j^{\top}\Sigma_{\mathrm{post}}(S)\,v_j=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(V_T\Sigma_{\mathrm{post}}(S)V_T^{\top}\bigr)$, a Bayesian V-optimal design criterion (the A-optimal criterion for the linear map $V_T$)~\citep{chaloner1995bayesian,mulder2009multidimensional}. We minimise it greedily over $S\subseteq R$, adding the benchmark with the largest decrease; each gain is a rank-one update (Sherman--Morrison). We write S6 for this rule with $T$ taken to be all benchmarks, which is what an evaluator who does not know which scores will matter would use; S6T takes $T$ to be the evaluation target set of Section~\ref{sec:protocol} and is reported separately. Greedy selection carries a guarantee through the submodularity ratio of the objective~\citep{das2011submodular,bian2017guarantees}, but the guarantee can be vacuous when noise is small, and we do not claim that greedy selection is optimal. The rule is classical; we do not claim it as a contribution.

\paragraph{Applicability and cost.}
The method needs a historical matrix with enough models and coverage to estimate $r$ factors and the noise levels, a new model whose run set contains at least $k$ benchmarks, and scores that are roughly linear in the latent factors. Its computational cost is the EM fit once per training set plus one greedy pass per new model, which is small next to running even one benchmark; the evaluator's cost is $k/N$ of the benchmarks.

shown.message:
I took all nine of `experiment-repo`'s answers on #6 into the paper. The corrections are on `dev` at 489155a, but they are not in PR #5 yet.

- **Floor by rank:** the paper had 4.99, 4.81 and 4.69, from an earlier run that used only 20 of the 50 splits. It now says 5.06 at the selected rank, 4.89 at rank 24 and 4.76 at each model's own best rank. The last is described as an optimistic reference, not a protocol.
- **Remainder:** the theory section no longer says the remainder separates estimation error from misspecification, because the data don't separate them. The results section keeps the synthetic study as the size of the estimation term only.
- **29% against 11–17%:** the results section now says this comparison is only qualitative. The synthetic target is all benchmarks not run, in standardised units, with no separate floor term.
- **Selection rules:** S1, S2 and S4 are now defined as `experiment-repo` states.
- **Synthetic generator:** the appendix now gives its settings.

The build still has 19 pages, References is still on page 9, and no "??" remain.

`paper-repo` `dev` still holds the old `results/floor_by_rank.csv`, so the paper's new floor numbers don't yet match a delivered file. I asked `experiment-repo` on #6 to deliver the 157dd0a file and `33_floor_rank.py`. I'll update `candidate-primary`, which will withdraw the existing approvals, once that lands, and then re-request reviews.

Still waiting on files for the inference-rule comparison (Table 3), adaptive against batch selection, and the Open LLM Leaderboard transfer check. The paper says nothing about them yet.
